name: Imām Birgivī
summary: Ottoman scholar of Birgi whose al-ʿAwāmil al-jadīda and Iẓhār al-asrār became the first two books of naḥw in the Ottoman madrasa.
bio: Birgivī Meḥmed Efendi settled in Birgi in western Anatolia, where he taught and wrote until his death in 981/1573.

His al-ʿAwāmil arranges naḥw as sixty governors, thirty governed words and ten states, and its examples teach belief and conduct as well as grammar. Iẓhār al-asrār follows it, and both are still read in Turkey and the Balkans.

sources.title: Imam Birgivi and his place in the Arabic language, İSAM
